failures.gap: Source variant not preserved, and no worked boundary. The entry calls itself the source's Lemmas 2--3 (handbook/parts/p15/huber-robust-location.tex line 60). It omits the source's Remark to Lemma 3 (Huber 1964, printed p.77, PDF p.5). That Remark lets the sign-change hypothesis on lambda be replaced by a weaker one: lambda exists and is finite at some xi_0 and does not vanish identically on a nondegenerate interval. Neither body 49-62 nor annex 46-83 states or derives this alternative hypothesis. The boundary it marks (lambda vanishing on an interval, where minimizing choices need not converge) is not worked. A grep finds the variant nowhere else in P15.

Source variant narrowed. The source's Winsorizing property (example (iii), printed p.79, PDF p.7) takes t_0 = T_n(x). It replaces each observation with |x_i - t_0| > k by the nearer of t_0 - k and t_0 + k, without changing the estimate T_n(x), and t_0 equals the modified mean. The entry (body 145-147) states only that, for any zero t_0, the score still vanishes at t_0 and t_0 is the modified mean. The annex (188-194) proves only that a minimizing location is preserved. It adds that the replacement 'need not preserve every tie-breaking rule for every modified sample'. The invariance of the estimate itself is neither stated nor proved: the modified sample's zero set is the single point t_0, so its midpoint estimate equals T_{n,k}(x).

Source variant narrowed: a promised case is missing. The source (Sec. 7, printed p.83, PDF p.11) says the bias bound is reached whenever H puts all its mass to the right of k + c, or to the left of -k - c. The entry states attainment only 'by contamination at any M > c_* + k' (body 286-287). The annex proves it only for H = delta_M, plus reflection (428-430). Attainment by every contaminant concentrated on [c_* + k, infinity), or its reflection, is neither stated nor proved. Yet handbook/parts/p15/robustness-and-sensitivity-of-inference-w02b-p15-071.tex lines 114-116 cite this entry for exactly that claim.
